title: How Kepler Built Verifiable AI for Financial Services — Vinoo Ganesh
talk_summary: Kepler's CEO argues that LLMs are probability machines that should never perform or persist numeric computation themselves; instead the model decides what to compute and hands off to deterministic tools, with atomic provenance, scope determinism, and replayable derivation chains. The talk is finance-specific but the core mechanism—separating non-deterministic reasoning from deterministic execution and verifying outputs against a canonical ledger—generalizes to any agent system.

takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM only selects which data to fetch and which computation to run; extraction, parsing, and math are done by deterministic code/databases outside the model's context, and the model never writes the number itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the model decides what to compute. It never does the computation itself.

takeaways.what_they_do: Any number that fails an independent deterministic check is stripped before reaching the user; verification is a repeatable mechanism, not another model grading another model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we can't verify it independently, we strip it out. That number will never make it to someone
takeaways.numbers: 94% extraction accuracy still rejected as insufficient

takeaways.technique: Provenance ledger / derivation chain per artifact
takeaways.what_they_do: Every produced value carries a reference to its source and the chain of transformations, replayable and rewindable, so any output can be audited back to primitives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need some kind of a chain of events to figure out what went into producing an individual number

takeaways.technique: Right tool for the right job (avoid token-maxing)
takeaways.what_they_do: Explicitly rejects spending multi-billion-parameter model cycles on tasks a CPU cycle can do; frames the next phase as cost optimization like the Snowflake/Databricks ROI wave.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sometimes you don't need a multi-billion parameter model when one CPU cycle will just work

takeaways.technique: Don't eval your way to determinism
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues evals cannot make a non-deterministic model deterministic; correctness must come from a deterministic substrate, not from benchmark scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You cannot take a non-deterministic LLM and eval your way to something deterministic.
